text:
alex: Quick sync request — running into a race between soft-offload compaction and streaming decode that briefly leaves GPU pointers invalid. Anyone seen this?

maria: Which codepath? streaming decode or batching? repro?

alex: Streaming decode (small tokens). Sequence: prefix cached in host, soft-offload marks pages movable, compaction kicks during decode, GPU kvcache ref becomes stale for ~10-30ms. No crash, but tail latency spike + internal retry.

devon: Do you have a log snippet or stack?

alex: Pasting minimal log:

```
[2025-11-12 14:02:13.123] tenant=acct-42 decode: kvcache.ref=0x7f8e4 valid=true
[2025-11-12 14:02:13.128] compactor: compact slab id=512 -> moved pages
[2025-11-12 14:02:13.130] tenant=acct-42 decode: kvcache.ref=0x7f8e4 valid=false -> rebind start
[2025-11-12 14:02:13.135] rebind: reading host copy -> remap to new GPU ptr
[2025-11-12 14:02:13.140] decode resumed (latency +18ms)
```

maria: Oh yeah. This is the soft-offload vs compaction window. Two high-level mitigations: 1) pin semantics (pin/unpin) for critical prefix ranges, 2) epoched handles so compaction increments epoch and old handles fail-fast.

casey: Pinning works but increases host residency, which hurts fairness under high load. Epoch handles are attractive: compactor bumps epoch, and reads check epoch before use. If mismatch -> fast rebind.

alex: Sketch of epoch handle idea:
```
struct Handle { ptr; epoch; tenant_id; }
use(handle) { if (handle.epoch != allocator.current_epoch(handle.tenant_id)) fail_and_rebind(); else proceed(); }
```

casey: Fail+rebind cost matters. If rebind is synchronous we get p99 regressions. Need a non-blocking repair path: trigger async rebind and optionally return cached shadow copy for one request.
sam: Right — want a stageless fallback: try fast validate -> if invalid, attempt lightweight read-copy -> return with a soft-degraded latency (e.g., +3ms) and simultaneously schedule full async remap. For big pages that's cheaper than full rebind.
maria: Also telemetry contract: increment counter on handle.invalidation, histogram for rebind latency buckets, per-tenant compaction frequency. We should surface in Console for SLA alerts.
devon: From allocator boundary POV we need explicit ops: alloc_handle.reserve(), alloc_handle.release(), alloc_handle.validate(epoch) and alloc_handle.refresh(). Keep ABI tiny.
alex: Agree. Also need to define semantics for cache prefetch/backoff: on validate failure do we immediately fetch host copy or try a small exponential backoff to avoid thundering rebinds?

casey: Use leader election per-tenant object: first thread doing rebind becomes leader and others wait on its completion with a short deadline; if leader stalls, others fall back to read-copy. That keeps remap work bounded.
sam: Perf targets: rebind tail should be <10ms for small objs (<=64KB) 95th, <30ms 99th. Read-copy path should be <5ms 99th. We'll need microbench and canary.

infra-bot: canary: started deploy "epoch-handles-v1" to 10% infra (tags: eng-runtime-canary).

maria: Nice. For API naming let's avoid "pin" for long-term. Maybe reserve()/release() to indicate intention (short-lived reservation). Pin sounds like a memory leak risk.
alex: Good point. reserve()/release() it is. Add a lease TTL on reserve to auto-release in case of client bug.
devon: One more edge: cross-tenant compaction where compactor moves pages between arenas — epoch must be tenant-scoped and compactor must acquire compaction token per-tenant to increment epoch atomically. Otherwise race where epoch increments then compactor moves pages but tenant still using old arena.

casey: So compactor flow: acquire tenant token -> snapshot current epoch -> perform move -> bump epoch -> release token. Readers validate against epoch; if mismatch -> rebind.
alex: I'll draft RFC including: API (reserve/release/validate/refresh), leader election pattern, read-copy fallback, telemetry metrics, perf targets, and compactor token protocol.
maria: Also include a migration plan: start with canary on low-QPS tenants, instrument error-rate and p99 latency, then widen.
sam: Don't forget GC of stale handles in C++ wrappers; we need weak refs in language bindings that auto-refresh on access.
alex: Will open RFC PR today and link perf microbench. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

casey: Thanks — looks like a sane path forward.
alex: Filing now: https://git.internal/r/redwood/rfcs/pulls/412 — please review when you get a sec.
